title: Vegetariansk potatissoppa (Vegetarian Potato Soup)
description: A soup made with potato, jerusalem artichokes, and celery.
steps: Peel the potato raw; peel the Jerusalem artichokes and celery root in the usual manner and put them on in cold, salted water.
When the root vegetables are soft, pass them through a sieve.
Melt 1.5 tablespoons of the butter with the flour, add the passed mass, and let the soup cook for 10-15 minutes, then taste and adjust seasoning.
Whip the egg yolks and cream in the soup bowl, add the cold butter, and mix the purée in with vigorous whisking.
Serve with toasted bread.

title: Vegetariska Lökdolmar (Vegetarian Onion Dolmas)
description: Prepared with onions, rice, and rusks.

ingredients.name: 2 cups vegetable broth or potato water

steps: Peel the onions, place in boiling salted water and let cook slowly without a lid about 7 minutes.
Remove and carefully loosen the layers and place on linen to drain.
For the forcemeat, use cold rice porridge.
Whip the eggs and mix into the porridge together with the rusks and clarified butter, then season well with salt, sugar and white pepper.
Place a teaspoon of forcemeat on each onion layer, roll up and tie with cotton twine, first dipped in hot water.
Brown the butter in an iron pot, add the dolmas and brown nicely, then thin with the boiling vegetable broth or potato water.
Place the lid on and let braise slowly about 30 minutes.
Place on a warm platter, cut off the twine and pour the sauce over. Serve as a breakfast dish with potato pudding or fried potatoes.

title: Vetebröd (enkelt) (Simple Wheat Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with wheat flour, yeast, and butter or margarine.
steps: Prepare the dough as described on page 462 (set aside a small amount of flour for rolling out) and allow it to rise to double its size.

title: Vetebröd (fint) (Fine Wheat Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with wheat flour, yeast, and sweet almonds.
steps: Sift the flour into a bowl, set aside a small amount for rolling out. Heat the milk to approximately 40 degrees and stir it into the flour together with the yeast, dissolved with the salt and 1 tsk. of the sugar, after which the dough is worked until it is smooth and glossy.
The dough can be rolled out into 15 round buns, in which a cross is made with a sharp knife.
Place the breads on buttered baking sheets, allow to rise for approximately 1 1/2 hours, brush with whipped egg or milk, sprinkle with poppy seeds and bake in a warm oven for 20-25 minutes.
The dough can also be rolled out into 30 thin sticks, which are cut diagonally, allowed to rise, brushed with milk, sprinkled with salt and baked until beautifully brown in a warm oven.
Instead of yeast, 2 teaspoons baking powder can be used, but the breads are then baked immediately they are rolled out.

title: Vetebröd (fint) (Fine Wheat Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with wheat flour, yeast, and sweet almonds.
steps: Sift the flour into a bowl, reserving a little for shaping. Heat the milk to about 40° and mix it into the flour along with the yeast, dissolved with salt and 1 tsp. of sugar, then work the dough until it is smooth and glossy.
Cover and let it rise to double its size.
Beat the butter with the sugar until fluffy, blend with the blanched and ground almonds and the egg, and add to the dough along with the finely crushed cardamom if desired.
Work the dough well and add more flour if the dough is too loose, then let it rise again.
Turn out onto a floured work surface, work well, and divide into 5 equal parts, which are shaped into wreaths or braids and placed on buttered baking sheets to rise.
Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with blanched and ground almonds mixed with pearl sugar, and bake in a hot oven until light and golden.

Alternatively, each part can be rolled out into a 1 cm thick square, brushed with melted butter, sprinkled with a mixture of blanched and ground sweet almonds, sanding sugar, and finely chopped candied citrus peel if desired, rolled tightly, and shaped as a roll or wreath with seam-side down on a buttered sheet.
Score the breads nicely, let them rise, and treat and bake as above.

Instead of baking the dough rolls whole, each can be cut into 12 pieces, placed seam-side down on buttered sheets, or pressed in the middle with the handle of a table knife, turned over, and placed on buttered sheets to rise, then treated and baked as above.

title: Veteskorpor (Wheat Rusks)
description: Prepared with cream, wheat flour, and yeast.
steps: Melt the cream in the milk — the rusks become thereby softer. — The dough is made and worked as in no. 950. When it has risen for the second time, knead the dough well on the work surface and divide into 10 equal parts. Each part is worked well and cut into 25—30 pieces. These are rolled into small rusks, which should be completely smooth and shiny when laid on the pan. They are covered, allowed to rise in a warm, draft-free place and baked in a warm oven. When the rusks are cold, they are cut in half and dried first in a not too warm oven, until they have taken on a beautiful light brown color, and then in weaker oven heat, until they are dry and soft. — The rusks can be made simpler by using skimmed milk and by reducing the butter and sugar.

title: Viltpastej (Game Pâté)
description: Prepared with lard, cream, and truffle.

ingredients.name: 2 msk. finely chopped truffle (for the mold)

steps: The scraped poultry is ground together with the lard 5 times through a meat grinder and then pounded with a wooden pestle in a stone mortar until a smooth and supple forcemeat.
The egg yolks are whisked with the flour and cream and this mixture is added tablespoon by tablespoon to the forcemeat, while it is worked for about 1 hour.
The forcemeat is carefully seasoned with the spices and lastly the egg whites, beaten to stiff peaks, are folded in.
A timbale mold is greased with butter and sprinkled with finely chopped truffle, the forcemeat is poured in and cooked slowly in a water bath for about 2 hours.

title: Vörtbröd (Malt Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with malt, wheat flour, and yeast.

ingredients.name: 1 1/2 litres malt (concentrated from 5 litres of malt)

steps: The day before the bread is to be baked, concentrate the malt, which takes about 6 hours

title: Vörtbröd (Spiced Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with wheat flour, yeast, and rye.
steps: The day before baking, prepare the wort, which takes about 6 hours.
In the evening, sift about 0.75 kg of the wheat flour (reserve the rest for shaping) into a large bowl or trough.
Mix the cold milk and yeast (dissolved with salt) into the flour and work the dough quickly.
Cover with a cloth and let it rest in a warm place overnight.
Early the next morning, warm the wort to about 40 degrees and add it to the yeast dough along with enough rye flour to make a firm dough.
Cover with a warm cloth and let it rise to double its size.
In a saucepan, mix the fat, syrup and spices, bring to a boil and cool.

When risen, turn the rolls onto a bread paddle, place on buttered, lukewarm baking sheets and let stand about 10 minutes.

Let dry briefly in the oven before removing and placing between cloths so the crust becomes soft.

The bread bakes best in a baking oven, which should be heated as soon as the dough is ready and swept clean as soon as the bread is shaped. The oven should remain completely closed until the bread is ready to bake.

title: Wienerbröd (Viennese Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with wheat flour, yeast, and sweet almonds.
steps: Sift the flour into a bowl and mix with the sugar.
Add the milk little by little together with the compressed yeast, mixed with salt and 1 teaspoon sugar.
Add the finely crushed cardamom.
Work the dough until it is smooth and glossy.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1 1/2 cm.
Place the butter in flakes on it and fold the dough in thirds, then fold again in thirds the same way as folding a napkin.
Roll out the dough again and fold in the same way, repeating this 3-4 times until the butter is well incorporated.
Let the dough rest about 1 hour in a cool place until it becomes firm.
Roll out to 1 cm thickness.
Cut into 1 1/2 cm wide strips with a pastry cutter, twist and form as rings, snails or braids and place on buttered baking sheets.
Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with blanched, finely chopped almonds and let rise slowly.
When well risen, sprinkle with sugar and bake in a very hot oven.
The dough can also be cut into diagonal squares.
When baked, the pastries can be brushed with water glaze flavored with vanilla or lemon.

title: À-la-Daube på Ål (Eel in Aspic)

title: Ägg med majonnäs i gelé (Eggs with Mayonnaise in Aspic)
description: Prepared with eggs, shrimp, and mustard.
steps: The mayonnaise should preferably be prepared the day before it is to be used to become sufficiently firm.
Separate the egg yolks from the whites (the whites and shells will be used for the aspic), place in a large bowl together with the spices and mustard and stir with a wooden spoon for 15 minutes.
Add the oil thereafter drop by drop, alternating with the vinegar and lemon juice; finally stir in the boiling water.

Shell the eggs, which should be cold, cut off the whites at the tips and cut each egg into 4 slices, which are placed on a deep plate.

Strain the stock through a cloth or napkin wrung out in hot water.
Let the clear aspic cool and pour it carefully over the garnished eggs.
When the dish has set, remove the egg slices with a round cutter so that a border of aspic extends beyond the egg edge.
Place them on an oval plate, garnish with parsley or salad and serve at the sandwich table.

title: Äggstruvor (Egg Fritters)
description: Prepared with egg yolk, cream, and lard.
steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar with a steel whisk for 20 minutes, then add the cream and the flour, which should be sifted, and stir the mixture well.
Heat the lard in a small iron saucepan, not larger than a saucer.
At the same time as the lard is placed in the saucepan, place the frying iron in it to warm it, otherwise the mixture will not stick to the iron.

When the lard is hot, dip the iron in the mixture and pour it into the hot lard until the fritter has a beautiful golden brown color, then loosen it with a larding pin and place it upside down on absorbent paper to drain.
Serve warm and dusted with sugar, if desired, with coffee or tea or as a dessert with jam or compote.
If there is no frying iron, pour 2 tbsp. of the mixture into a funnel and ring it back and forth in the lard, so that it forms a broken cake according to the size of the saucepan.

When the fritter has a beautiful golden brown color on the underside, turn it with a lard spoon, and when it is even in color, place it on absorbent paper, over a stick, if desired, so that the fritter becomes bent.

title: Äkta majonnäs (True Mayonnaise)
description: Prepared with egg yolks, grains, and tarragon or vinegar.
steps: Place the egg yolks in a large bowl together with the seasonings and stir with a wooden spoon for 10 minutes.
Gradually pour the vinegar over the yolks with vigorous stirring.
When the vinegar is blended with the yolks, add the oil in a thin stream with constant stirring.
Finish the sauce with lemon juice and the boiling water—the latter to prevent it from breaking.
Mayonnaise prepared in this way is quite thin and should therefore stand in a cool (not too cold) place for 4—5 hours to thicken.
It can be stored for 3—4 days without damage, provided it is well covered and does not stand on ice.
If the sauce breaks, this can be remedied by gradually stirring it into 1 egg yolk and 1/2 tablespoon vinegar.
The sauce becomes lighter if mustard is omitted and only lemon juice is used instead of vinegar.

Strain through a cloth wrung out in hot water, carefully remove all fat from the sauce, bring to a boil, and taste for seasoning.
Cut the bird, garnish with small sausages, vegetables, and browned potatoes.
Serve the sauce in a sauce boat.

Cut out a lid for the mold, brush the mold's edge with water and cover with a thick strip of dough, which is pressed firmly on the edge and brushed with water.
Place the dough lid on and press firmly against the mold's inner edge, then smooth the outer edges of the lid and strip with a sharp knife.
Crimp the edge with the back of the knife and flute with the point of the knife.

title: Äppelpaj med smördeg (Apple Pie with Butter Pastry for 6)
description: A pastry dish made with pastry, butter, and brandy.
steps: Sift the flour on a pastry board, wash the butter and distribute finely in the flour, working it in with fingertips.
Then quickly add the brandy, and as soon as the dough is cohesive, set it aside to become cold.
Peel the apples, remove the cores and cut into thin slices and place in a heatproof mold with sugar between each layer.
The last layer should be fruit.
If the apples are not juicy, add 0.5 cup water.
Roll out the pie dough to 0.5 cm. thickness.
Cut a lid for the mold, brush the edge of the mold with water and cover with a thick strip of dough, which is pressed firmly on the edge and brushed with water.
Place the dough lid on and press firmly against the inner edge of the mold, then trim the outer edges of the lid and strip with a sharp knife.
Prick the edge with the back of the knife and crimp with the tip of the knife.
Make four holes in the lid with a coarse whisk.
Brush the pie with beaten egg and place in good oven heat to bake until beautifully golden brown for about 1 hour.
Serve warm or cold with whipped cream.
